device.note: 15% a year expected return; hold up to 3 years.

other.note: 15% a year expected return; hold up to 3 years.

rules.sellFloorNote: Sell or trim when the expected return from today's price falls below this (it pays better elsewhere).

pos.source: Approximate Phase 3 (or pivotal) success rates, rounded from published industry studies (BIO/Informa/QLS 2011–2020 and similar). Rough starting points — edit freely.

samePos3.label: Same drug already won a Phase 3

poorClass.label: Drug class has a poor record

reactions.source: Rough rules of thumb for ASX small/mid-cap healthcare stocks, not one study. The app shows each stock's own measured moves as they build up — trust those more over time.

rare.title: Rare-disease operator scorecard
rare.source: Built from public descriptions of David R. Craig, The New Rules of Rare Disease (2026): small populations, incomplete natural-history data, uncertain endpoints, unconventional funding, finding scattered patients, capital efficiency and milestone-based financing. Not the book's own checklist.
items: Is the primary endpoint agreed with FDA and backed by natural-history data?
Registries, advocacy-group ties, trial recruitment speed.
Orphan, Rare Pediatric (voucher), Breakthrough, accelerated approval.
Royalties, grants, partner cash rather than share issues.
Funded to the next value step
Cash covers the company past its next big readout?
Scalable product supply locked in before it is needed.
Credible buyers or partners for the asset.
Spending on the work that moves value; promises kept.

device.title: Device commercialisation scorecard
device.source: Mehta, Commercializing Successful Biomedical Technologies (2nd ed., 2022): ch.2 market and referral chain, ch.5 device stage-gate and failure modes, ch.6 FDA pathways, ch.7 manufacturing, ch.8 reimbursement.
items: Does the result change a clinical decision or outcome?
510(k) / De Novo / PMA chosen and FDA meetings held.
Coding, coverage and payment for the device or procedure.
End user and referral chain fit
Who decides, who pays, fits the workflow.
Design for manufacture, ISO 13485, production units.
Patents and licences protect the product.
Cash and non-dilutive funding vs burn.
Alternatives (e.g. CT, existing devices) and switching cost.

other.title: Drug commercialisation scorecard
other.source: Mehta, Commercializing Successful Biomedical Technologies (2nd ed., 2022): ch.5 drug failure modes (ADME 41%, efficacy 31%, toxicity 22%, business 6%), ch.6 FDA pathways incl. 505(b)(2), ch.7 scale-up, ch.4 IP/licensing, ch.8 reimbursement.
items: Efficacy, safety and drug-property (ADME) risks addressed by data.
Who prescribes, competing products, real need.
Patent life, freedom to operate, licence terms.
Cash vs burn to the next value step.
Partner vs go-it-alone suits the asset.
